nodes.label: bsm_agent: LLM-Assisted BSM Model Building Framework
nodes.author: Shaikh Saad
nodes.rationale: Open-source Python framework combining deterministic symbolic backend for beyond-Standard-Model physics with LLM chat interface for natural-language model construction.

nodes.label: Field and Group Representation Layer
nodes.rationale: Defines field classes and group-representation utilities for Standard Model quantum numbers under SU(3)_c × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y; distinguishes scalar and Weyl-fermion types.

nodes.label: Model Construction Layer
nodes.rationale: Initializes SM field content and extends with additional scalar/fermionic fields; generates complete renormalizable gauge-invariant operator basis automatically.

nodes.label: Component Field Expansion Layer
nodes.rationale: Expands gauge-invariant operators into explicit component fields using SU(2) and SU(3) index contractions with Clebsch-Gordan coefficients.

nodes.label: EWSB and Mass-Matrix Layer
nodes.rationale: Assigns VEVs to neutral color-singlet scalars; derives stationary conditions and tree-level mass matrices from shifted Lagrangian.

nodes.label: Report Generation Layer
nodes.rationale: Generates compact and fully expanded LaTeX representations of models directly from symbolic backend; produces PDF-ready output.

nodes.label: LLM Agent Orchestration Layer
nodes.rationale: Connects model-building tools to conversational backend; manages intent matching, tool routing, confirmation workflows; LLM never generates physics outputs.

nodes.label: Tool-Calling Interface Design
nodes.rationale: LLM interprets natural-language requests, translates to structured field schema, asks clarification questions, selects appropriate backend tools, formats output.

nodes.label: Conversation State and Confirmation Workflow
nodes.rationale: Maintains conversation history and model state; infers candidate interpretations and requests confirmation before model creation to prevent errors from ambiguous input.

nodes.label: Provider Layer: Local, Remote, Commercial
nodes.rationale: Backend-agnostic separation supporting local Ollama, remote self-hosted servers, and commercial APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic); enables switching without modifying symbolic code.

nodes.label: Gauge Anomaly Checking
nodes.rationale: Computes standard anomaly coefficients by summing over left-handed Weyl fermions; reports whether all five coefficients vanish; suggests conjugate representations if needed.

nodes.label: Automatic Renormalizable Operator Generation
nodes.rationale: Enumerates all scalar monomials up to four fields; tests gauge singlet condition and mass dimension ≤4; generates scalar potential, fermion mass, and Yukawa sectors automatically.

nodes.label: Computational Scaling with Large Representations
nodes.rationale: Runtime depends on representation sizes; larger SU(2)_L and SU(3)_c multiplets require longer execution; includes representation-aware optimizations for common cases.

nodes.label: Supported Gauge Representations
nodes.rationale: SU(2)_L dimensions 1-7 (motivated by minimal dark matter); SU(3)_c singlet, triplet, antitriplet, sextet, antisextet, octet (motivated by SO(10) GUTs); arbitrary U(1)_Y hypercharge.

nodes.label: Leptoquark Model Case Study
nodes.rationale: Complete end-to-end example demonstrating model construction, anomaly checking, Lagrangian expansion, and mass matrix extraction for leptoquark BSM extension.

nodes.label: Standard Model Template
nodes.rationale: Built-in SM field content serves as starting point for BSM extensions; package can generate SM reports, expand Lagrangian, and derive mass matrices.

nodes.label: Right-Handed Neutrino Extension Model
nodes.rationale: Simple BSM model example: SM extended with fermion singlet (1,1,0); demonstrates natural-language model specification and automatic Lagrangian generation.

nodes.label: SymPy Symbolic Backend
nodes.rationale: Python symbolic mathematics library used for deterministic physics calculations; ensures reproducibility and correctness of model-building results.

nodes.label: Ollama Local LLM Inference
nodes.rationale: Primary intended deployment mode; runs LLM locally on user's machine; supports models like gpt-oss:20b and qwen3.5:35b without external API calls.

nodes.label: LangChain Integration
nodes.rationale: Uses langchain-core and langchain-ollama for LLM orchestration; enables tool-calling interface and conversation management.

nodes.label: Complementarity to SARAH, FeynRules, Susyno
nodes.rationale: bsm_agent automates early model-building stage (operator generation from quantum numbers); complements downstream tools that derive vertices, mass spectra from specified Lagrangian.

nodes.label: Reliability Principle: LLM Never Generates Physics
nodes.rationale: Core design principle: LLM serves only as orchestration layer; all physics outputs (Lagrangian, anomaly coefficients, mass matrices) generated by deterministic backend.

nodes.label: BSM Agent Package
nodes.rationale: AI-driven natural-language interface for Beyond Standard Model physics construction, combining LLM orchestration with symbolic computation for automated Lagrangian generation and anomaly checking.

nodes.label: LLM Natural Language Interface
nodes.rationale: Enables users to specify BSM field quantum numbers in natural language rather than rigid syntax, serving as orchestration layer between user and deterministic symbolic engine.

nodes.label: Symbolic Computation Engine
nodes.rationale: Core deterministic backend performing group-theoretical operator generation, anomaly detection, and Lagrangian expansion independent of LLM, preserving reproducibility and scientific rigor.

nodes.label: Operator Generation Module
nodes.rationale: Constructs all independent interaction terms (kinetic, Yukawa, scalar potential) using group-theoretical rules; output depends only on group theory, free from arbitrariness.

nodes.label: Anomaly Detection Module
nodes.rationale: Verifies gauge anomaly cancellation (SU(3), SU(2), U(1) cubic and gravitational); provides hints for anomaly resolution when models are anomalous.

nodes.label: Lagrangian Expansion Module
nodes.rationale: Expands compact operator notation into component fields with explicit SU(3) and SU(2) indices; output depends on basis, normalization, and phase conventions chosen by user.

nodes.label: Mass Matrix Generator
nodes.rationale: Extracts and diagonalizes mass matrices from scalar potential and Yukawa sectors for phenomenological analysis.

nodes.label: Scalar Leptoquark Model Example
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates package capability: 5 scalar leptoquarks with 14 kinetic terms, 73 scalar potential terms, 14 Yukawa terms, 49 mixed BSM interactions, all generated in <2 seconds.

nodes.label: Basis and Normalization Conventions
nodes.rationale: Package uses canonical field normalization, no numerical prefactors in coupling coefficients, and phase conventions that preserve physical predictions; users must map their conventions to package conventions for meaningful comparison.

nodes.label: Natural Language Quantum Number Parsing
nodes.rationale: Accepts multiple equivalent natural-language descriptions of quantum numbers (e.g., 'bar 6', 'anti-sextet', 'color anti 6') and normalizes to canonical form for validation.

nodes.label: Model State Management
nodes.rationale: Supports incremental model building: users can clear, extend, or reset models via natural-language commands; enables iterative exploration of BSM parameter space.

nodes.label: SymPy Symbolic Backend
nodes.rationale: Underlying symbolic computation library for algebraic manipulation and Lagrangian expansion.

nodes.label: LangChain Orchestration Layer
nodes.rationale: Framework for routing natural-language user input to appropriate symbolic computation modules.

nodes.label: Ollama LLM Runtime
nodes.rationale: Open-source LLM inference engine enabling local deployment of language interface without proprietary API dependency.

nodes.label: Symbolic AI Integration with LLMs
nodes.rationale: Paradigm: LLMs serve as interface/orchestration layer for deterministic symbolic engines; preserves transparency, reproducibility, and scientific rigor while improving accessibility.

nodes.label: Beyond Standard Model Construction
nodes.rationale: Physics workflow: specify new field quantum numbers → generate all renormalizable interactions → check anomaly cancellation → expand Lagrangian → extract mass matrices; traditionally manual and error-prone.
